saml.description: External IdP logins may create a new account or link to an existing ZITADEL account based on configured manual/automatic linking options and criteria such as username or email.
saml.note: Identity merges caused by configured linking are by design and must be controlled during collision tests.

saml.description: If organization-specific settings override defaults, the client must send the organization scope in the authorization request to get the expected branding, policies, and IdP selection.
saml.note: Missing org scope can change which IdPs are available and which policies apply, causing misleading login outcomes.

saml.description: SAML endpoint errors may still be returned with HTTP 200 while the SAML payload contains an error StatusCode and message.
saml.note: HTTP 200 alone does not indicate successful SAML processing.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows; unsolicited IdP-initiated responses are not supported.
saml.note: Do not report lack of IdP-initiated support as a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint can return HTTP 200 even when the SAML operation failed; the actual failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: Success/failure must be determined from SAML content, not HTTP status alone.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, ZITADEL places it in the access_token response field and marks token_type as N_A.
saml.note: This is RFC-driven behavior and should not be treated as token confusion.

saml.description: The userinfo endpoint accepts the user's access token, not the id_token, as Bearer credential.
saml.note: Using an id_token for verify_granted_identity will fail by design.

saml.description: ZITADEL may issue opaque access tokens by default and JWT access tokens only when configured or requested via token exchange.
saml.note: Differences in token format alone are by design and not evidence of inconsistent identity binding.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL as broker/SP behavior; a valid SAML test must begin with the SP/OIDC authorization flow so ZITADEL creates request state before the upstream SAML response is processed.

For SAML-brokered login tests, the fuzzer MUST drive the browser/OIDC flow through /oauth/v2/authorize and complete /oauth/v2/token. The upstream SAML assertion is not exchanged directly for an API bearer token; ZITADEL finishes login and then issues OIDC/OAuth tokens. Use access_token as session_token, not id_token.

To force a specific SAML external IdP during login, include reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}. If organization-specific login policy is configured, also include the organization scope (for example urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}) or ZITADEL may be unable to identify the intended IdP and the test result will be ambiguous.

For SAML custom-login or proxied SAML tests, preserve all original query parameters when proxying to ZITADEL and keep the request state intact. ZITADEL binds the flow to created request state (for example authRequest / SAML request IDs); dropping or rewriting parameters can cause false I3 failures unrelated to security.

Do not infer SAML login success or failure from HTTP status alone on the SAML endpoint. ZITADEL documents that SAML errors can still return HTTP 200 with an error StatusCode inside the SAML response. Tests that inspect only HTTP status will misclassify failures as successes.

For I2 freshness/replay tests on SAML-brokered sessions, include a control login through the same OIDC flow using a valid baseline configuration. A failed browser/token flow can result from missing org scope, disabled external login policy, or missing user-creation mapping rather than the replay/freshness condition under test.

Login V2 SAML brokering may fail to create users unless required fields are mapped from SAML attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. If this mapping is absent, treat user-creation failure as setup error, not as a security rejection.

For I4 identity-binding tests, ZITADEL can be configured to auto-link or manually link external identities to existing accounts by username or email. A SAML login that lands on an existing account because of configured linking is by design and must not be flagged as a collision unless the test first disables/controls linking behavior.

For I3 config-change tests involving external IdPs or login policy, NEW logins after an admin changes provider activation, login policy, or org-scoped settings are expected to follow the updated configuration. Do not flag this as incoherence; a valid I3 test must show inconsistent handling of the same request state, not a legitimate policy change affecting later logins.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 token-exchange audience tests, first obtain the necessary audience in the original login token via reserved project audience scopes; otherwise rejection is expected setup behavior, not an authorization-binding bug.
Token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target behavior. Do NOT use resource to test authorization narrowing/broadening on ZITADEL.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns that ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that value as a bearer session token for subsequent API calls; use requested_token_type access_token or jwt when a usable session token is required.

ZITADEL may issue opaque access tokens by default. For verification and access tests, use the returned access_token as bearer and rely on /oidc/v1/userinfo or introspection semantics rather than assuming JWT structure. Parsing failures are not security failures.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and obtain a valid SAML request / request ID before attempting saml_login; unsolicited IdP-initiated SAML responses are not a valid test setup for this platform.

For saml_login, the executor MUST preserve the exact SAML request context (including request ID / InResponseTo and RelayState) from the initiated flow. ZITADEL's SAML flow is request-bound and finalized by updating /v2/saml/saml_requests/{saml_request_id} with a session; sending a fabricated response without matching request context will be rejected for flow reasons, not because the attack was detected.

SAML endpoint /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on protocol-level errors; failures are conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not via HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML exchanges as success by itself, or it will create false positives/negatives for I1/I5 tests.

For SAML broker tests that end in OIDC tokens, verify_granted_identity MUST use the access_token from /oauth/v2/token, not the id_token. ZITADEL's userinfo endpoint requires the user access token as Bearer credential.

When testing organization-scoped SAML login behavior, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} if organization-specific login policy or IdP configuration is being exercised. Otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and the result will not reflect the intended tenant-specific SAML configuration.

For direct-to-external-IdP SAML broker tests, the authorization request MAY use reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id} to force redirection to a specific configured external IdP. If omitted, UI selection or domain discovery may choose a different IdP and invalidate the test setup.

Login V2 user creation from external SAML IdPs requires required user fields to be populated. Without an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent (or equivalent mapping), first-time SAML logins can fail because required fields are missing. The fuzzer MUST provision attribute mapping/action support or use already-linkable users when testing broker acceptance logic.

For I4 cross-protocol or SAML email-binding collision tests, ZITADEL may create or link users based on external IdP information and configured linking/creation options. The fuzzer MUST control whether it is testing new-user creation versus linking to an existing account; otherwise an apparent identity merge may be by configured account-linking behavior rather than a broker flaw.

For I2 token-freshness control tests around the OIDC wrapper flow, include a control authorization-code exchange using a valid session/login path. A failed attack-path login can result from missing org scope, missing external IdP enablement, or missing attribute-mapping actions rather than the freshness property under test.

Token exchange audience handling is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target project/application; otherwise rejection is expected by design and not evidence of correct downstream audience enforcement.

Token exchange does not support the resource parameter; supplying resource always results in invalid_target behavior. The fuzzer MUST use audience, not resource, for I5 token-exchange audience tests on ZITADEL.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer API credential or interpret resulting failures as authorization bugs.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For I2 freshness tests involving token exchange, an expired subject ID token is expected to fail before any downstream authorization logic is reached.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow first and obtain a SAML request context before attempting any SAML response/finalization step; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML broker tests against ZITADEL as SP, user creation in Login V2 can fail unless required user fields are mapped from upstream SAML attributes. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream assertion provides required attributes (at least email/first/last name as shown in guides) or preconfigure an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent; otherwise login failures are setup failures, not security findings.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' in the relevant instance or organization login policy before testing SAML brokering; otherwise SAML login can be blocked by policy rather than by assertion validation.

SAML provider availability is separate from provider creation. After configuring a SAML IdP, the fuzzer MUST activate/link the provider to the login policy; an unactivated provider will not be usable for login and would cause false negatives.

When testing organization-specific SAML IdP behavior, the authorization request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and a different IdP/policy set, causing false positives or false negatives in I3/I4/I5 tests.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on protocol-level errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not via HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as success by itself when evaluating SAML protocol behavior.

For custom-login/UI mediated SAML flows, finalizing a SAML request requires an authorization header from an account with IAM_LOGIN_CLIENT role. If this role is missing, finalize/create-response failures are authorization/setup errors, not SAML security findings.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, audience in token exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. The fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience; otherwise rejection is by design and not an audience-binding vulnerability.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL may return scopes that differ from the requested scope after validation. The fuzzer MUST compare the returned scope and claims in the exchanged token, not just whether the request was accepted.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based client authentication or JWT profile grants, client assertion / JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Otherwise token endpoint rejection is expected setup failure, not a freshness or signature-validation bug.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 Profile grant type. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt to submit SAML assertions to /oauth/v2/token as a SAML bearer grant; only browser SAML and OIDC/token-exchange flows are valid here.

For introspection/userinfo-based verification, the requesting client must be part of the token audience. If not, inactive/invalid results are by design. The fuzzer MUST ensure the verification client is in audience before interpreting failures as authorization bugs.
